result.rationale:
The diff shows the zoho-bigin call site passes `credentialId` as the third arg to refreshOAuthTokens (`"zoho-bigin",
      credentialId`) while every other call site (google-calendar, hubspot, lark-calendar, office365-calendar, msteams, webex, zohocrm, zoomvideo) passes `credential.userId`. refreshOAuthTokens sends this value as `calcomUserId: userId.toString()` to the sync endpoint, so Bigin would transmit a credential id where a user id is expected. Real, verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

judged_text: The bigin call site passes `credentialId` — the credential row's id — as the userId argument where all seven other call sites in this diff pass `credential.userId`, so the sync endpoint receives `calcomUserId=<credential.id>`. The parent resolves credentials by its own user ids, which overlap the child instance's credential-id space, so Bigin users get another user's synced credentials written into their credential record (cross-user credential contamination) or no credentials at all.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the 3rd parameter is `userId` and (when syncing is enabled) it is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the call site passes `credentialId` as that 3rd argument (`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`), while the other integrations in this diff consistently pass `credential.userId`. Unless `credentialId` is actually the user id (which its name strongly suggests it is not), this will cause the sync endpoint to receive the wrong `calcomUserId` and return/update the wrong credentials.
